facts.reason: Values are correct, but in the 2021 IRC the 4-1/2 in handrail projection limit sits in the new R311.7.8.2 (Handrail projection), per Montana DLI 2021 IRC means of egress training; add it to the citation.

Missing the commonly tested exception in the model 2021 IRC R311.7.6: a landing is not required at the top of an interior flight (including stairs in an enclosed garage) when a door does not swing over the stairs (Montana DLI 2021 IRC means of egress training quotes the exception).

fixed.fact: Under the 2021 IRC, every stairway needs a floor or landing at the top and bottom. A landing must be at least as wide as the stair it serves, and on a straight run it must be at least 36 in deep in the direction of travel. Exception: no landing is needed at the top of an interior flight of stairs (including stairs in an enclosed garage) as long as a door does not swing over the stairs.

facts.reason: In the 2021 IRC the handrail subsections were renumbered: R311.7.8.2 is now Handrail projection and continuity is R311.7.8.4 (Montana DLI 2021 IRC means of egress training lists R311.7.8.1 height, .2 projection, .3 clearance, .4 continuity, .5 grip size).

The 2021 IRC changed R312.2.1 to measure to the bottom of the window's clear opening rather than the top of the sill (Philadelphia PB-031 2021 IRC Significant Changes FAQ, R312.2). Wording updated; the 24 in / 72 in values are correct.

fixed.fact: Under the 2021 IRC, an operable window needs fall protection when the bottom of its clear opening is less than 24 in above the finished floor and more than 72 in above the finished grade or other surface outside. The window must either not open far enough to pass a 4-in sphere or have an ASTM F2090 fall prevention device or window opening control device, and an opening control device on a required escape window must still give the full required escape opening once it is released.
fixed.note: The 2021 IRC measures both heights to the bottom of the clear opening; the 2018 and earlier editions measured to the top of the sill. Values confirmed by a 2021 IRC-based tip sheet (MyBuildingPermit TS 23) and the Philadelphia 2021 IRC significant changes FAQ.

facts.reason: The 2021 IRC R310.2.4 requires the path from an escape opening under a deck, porch or cantilever to be at least 36 in high AND 36 in wide (Boulder County B10 handout quoting 2021 IRC R310.2.4; Philadelphia 2021 IRC significant changes FAQ notes the new 36-in width).

fixed.fact: Under the 2021 IRC, an emergency escape opening may open under a deck, porch or cantilever only if the window can open fully and there is a path at least 36 in high and 36 in wide to a yard or court.

facts.reason: In the 2021 IRC the cooking-appliance distances are in R314.3.1 (not R314.3), and the 20/10/6 ft ionization/photoelectric scheme is the IRC text, not NFPA 72-2019 29.11.3.4 (which uses a 10-ft exclusion zone and nuisance-resistant listing). The 2021 R314.3.1 also has a fourth item for alarms listed to reduce cooking nuisance alarms (Anne Arundel County MD 2021 IRC smoke alarm handout quoting R314.3.1). The 2024 IRC deleted these distance rules.

fixed.fact: Under the 2021 IRC (R314.3.1), smoke alarms must be kept back from permanently installed cooking appliances unless that would prevent a required location: at least 20 ft for ionization alarms, 10 ft for ionization alarms with an alarm-silencing switch, and 6 ft for photoelectric alarms or alarms listed and marked to help reduce cooking nuisance alarms.
fixed.note: Confirmed by a 2021 IRC smoke alarm handout (Anne Arundel County, MD) quoting R314.3.1. The 2024 IRC removed these technology-based distances.

facts.reason: Wrong for CO alarms. Model 2021 IRC R315.2.2 exempts only plumbing work and work on mechanical systems that are NOT fuel-fired; work on a fuel-fired mechanical system triggers CO alarms (Anne Arundel County 2021 IRC CO alarm handout quoting R315.2.2; Philadelphia 2021 IRC significant changes FAQ). The smoke alarm exceptions in R314.2.2 (plumbing or mechanical) are stated correctly.

fixed.fact: When permitted alterations, repairs or additions are made to an existing home (2021 IRC), the house must get smoke alarms, and CO alarms where required, like a new dwelling. Work limited to exterior surfaces (roofing, siding, windows, doors, porches, decks) and plumbing work is exempt from both. Mechanical work is exempt from the smoke alarm rule, but for CO alarms only work on mechanical systems that are not fuel-fired is exempt, so work on a fuel-fired furnace or boiler triggers CO alarms.

facts.reason: The 2021 IRC R302.5.1 adds that garage-to-dwelling doors must be self-latching as well as self-closing or automatic-closing ('Doors shall be self-latching and equipped with a self-closing or automatic-closing device', quoted in Montgomery County MD 2021 IRC code changes webinar; also Sussex County DE and Philadelphia 2021 IRC change summaries).

fixed.fact: Under the 2021 IRC, a garage may not open directly into a room used for sleeping. Other doors between the garage and the house must be solid wood or solid or honeycomb-core steel at least 1-3/8 in thick, or 20-minute fire-rated, and must be self-latching and equipped with a self-closing or automatic-closing device.

facts.reason: Duplicate: existing KB fact DUCT-002 (IRC 2021 R302.5.2) already states the No. 26 gage sheet steel / no openings into the garage rule almost word for word. Content is otherwise correct.

Duplicate: existing KB facts GENE-011 and GENE-012 (IRC 2021 R602.6) already cover the 25/40 percent notch limits, 40/60 percent bored-hole limits, doubled studs with no more than two successive bored, and the 5/8 in edge distance. Content is correct; question 14 is still answerable from those facts.

Misstates the rule. Since the 2015 IRC, R311.8.1 limits only ramps serving the required egress door (R311.2) to 1:12 (1:8 where technically infeasible); all other ramps may be up to 1:8. R311.8.2 landings are measured as width perpendicular to the ramp slope, at least 36 in (2015 Michigan Residential Code R311.8 text; Montana DLI 2021 IRC training notes the 1:8 limit for other ramps; 2018 IRC Conejos County guide).

fixed.fact: Under the IRC, a ramp serving the required egress door may slope no more than 1 in 12 (8.3 percent), or 1 in 8 where site limits make that technically infeasible; all other ramps may slope up to 1 in 8 (12.5 percent). Ramps need a floor or landing at least 36 in wide (perpendicular to the slope) at the top and bottom, where doors open onto the ramp and where it changes direction, and a handrail on at least one side when the slope is steeper than 1 in 12.
fixed.note: R311.8.1 text confirmed in the 2015 Michigan Residential Code (same as the 2018 and 2021 IRC); Montana DLI 2021 IRC training also lists 1:12 for the egress ramp and 1:8 for other ramps.

facts.reason: The R303.7 exception is for 'remote, central or automatic control of lighting', not lights that are on continuously (Montana DLI 2021 IRC training quotes the exception).

fixed.fact: Interior stairways must have lighting able to light the treads and landings to at least 1 footcandle, measured at the center of the treads and landings. Where a stair has six or more risers, a wall switch is required at each floor level unless remote, central or automatic control of the lighting is provided.

facts.reason: Misleading by omission and the note is wrong: the one-half mezzanine allowance is a MODEL 2021 IBC exception, not a Seattle amendment. Model 505.2.1 Exception 2 allows one-half in Type I or II buildings with NFPA 13 sprinklers and an emergency voice/alarm system, and Exception 3 allows one-half for a mezzanine in a dwelling unit in a sprinklered building (2021 IBC 505.2.1 text reproduced in Houston's 2021 code changes; Code Red Consultants summary).

fixed.fact: Under the 2021 IBC, the total area of mezzanines in a room may not exceed one-third of that room's floor area, and mezzanines need at least 7 ft of clear height above and below. Exceptions raise the limit to two-thirds for special industrial occupancies in Type I or II construction, and to one-half in Type I or II buildings with a full NFPA 13 sprinkler system and an emergency voice/alarm communication system (or for a mezzanine inside a dwelling unit in a sprinklered building).
fixed.note: Confirmed against the 2021 IBC 505.2.1 text (Houston 2021 code changes reproduction) and Code Red Consultants. The one-half allowance is a model-code exception, not a local amendment.

facts.reason: Time-sensitive. eeoc.gov still lists federal contractors with 50+ employees, but that lower threshold came from Executive Order 11246, which was revoked Jan. 21, 2025; Morgan Lewis and DirectEmployers (May 2026) report the 50-99 contractor obligation is gone, and on May 14, 2026 the EEOC sent OMB a proposed rule to rescind EEO-1 through EEO-5 reporting (not final; the 100-employee requirement remains for now).

fixed.fact: The annual EEO-1 report of workforce demographics is required of private employers with 100 or more employees. Federal contractors with 50 to 99 employees used to file too, but that rule came from Executive Order 11246, which was revoked in January 2025. In May 2026 the EEOC proposed rescinding EEO-1 reporting altogether, so check the current year's filing instructions.
fixed.source: EEOC EEO data collections (EEO-1 Component 1); 29 CFR 1602.7; EO 14173 (2025)
fixed.note: eeoc.gov still mentions federal contractors with 50+ employees; law firm summaries (Morgan Lewis, May 2026) say that obligation ended with the revocation of EO 11246. The EEOC's proposed rescission had not been finalized as of mid-2026.

facts.reason: Misleading: the Form 4562 instructions put 'office furniture and equipment' in 7-year property but list typewriters, calculators, copiers and duplicating equipment (and computers, per Pub 946 asset class 00.12) as 5-year property. Students could wrongly class a computer or copier as 7-year.

fixed.fact: Under MACRS, automobiles, light general-purpose trucks, computers and office machines such as copiers and calculators are 5-year property; office furniture and fixtures (desks, files, safes) are 7-year property; residential rental buildings (80 percent or more of rent from dwelling units) are 27.5-year property; and nonresidential real property is 39-year property. Land is never depreciated.
fixed.source: IRS Instructions for Form 4562; IRS Pub 946 (Table B-1 asset classes 00.11-00.13)

questions.reason: The 2021 IRC R312.2.1 measures to the bottom of the window's clear opening, not the sill (Philadelphia 2021 IRC significant changes FAQ). Answer (72 in) unchanged.

fixed.q: Under the 2021 IRC, window fall protection is required when the bottom of an operable window's clear opening is less than 24 in above the floor and more than how high above the grade outside?
fixed.why: R312.2.1 applies where the bottom of the clear opening is under 24 in above the finished floor and more than 72 in above the finished grade or surface below.

questions.reason: The 20/10/6 ft distances are in 2021 IRC R314.3.1; NFPA 72-2019 29.11.3.4 uses a different (10-ft exclusion and nuisance-listing) scheme.

fixed.why: R314.3.1 keeps ionization alarms at least 20 ft from a permanently installed cooking appliance (10 ft with a silencing switch); photoelectric alarms need 6 ft.
